A stock count for an item at a location uses a new type called stock_level and stores the count date, the counted quantity, the book quantity — calculated as the sum of that item's stock movements into the location minus those out of it up to and including the count date — and the difference, which is counted minus book.

So when you do a stock count for an item at a location, right, you're creating a record of type stock_level, and that record's got the count date on it, the counted quantity, the book quantity — and the book quantity is basically all the stock movements for that item going into the location added up, then you take away all the ones going out, but only the ones dated up to and including the count date — and then finally you've got the difference, which is just counted minus book.

Each stock count of an item at a location gets recorded under a new type, stock_level, capturing four things: the count date; the counted quantity; the book quantity, being the sum of inbound stock movements for that item at that location less the outbound ones, all dated no later than the count date; and the difference, counted minus book.
